_comment: Betting-market team strength, used as a prior on the season projection.
Copy to rosters/market_odds_<target_year>.json and edit. The market is the
best single forward-looking read on team talent available: it knows
front-office intent, depth behind the starters, managerial quality, spring
injuries, and every signing that has not produced a stat line yet -- none
of which a roster aggregate can see.
WHICH MARKET -- use win totals.
win_total     THE ONE TO USE, and the default. A direct read on expected
wins: no inference, no probability-to-wins curve to invent.
division      One playoff round removed. Usable.
pennant       Two rounds removed.
world_series  Usable but the loosest. A title is four short series deep,
so playoff randomness compresses the board -- even the best
team in baseball wins it only 15-20% of the time. The top
of the board SATURATES and carries less talent information
than the middle. Futures are therefore used only for their
ORDERING and relative spacing, with the absolute scale
taken from MLB's own win distribution. Win totals need
none of that.
Because win totals are so much tighter, they get a higher default blend
weight (0.70) than futures (0.40). See MARKET_WEIGHT_BY_MARKET.
GIVE THE PRICES, NOT JUST THE LINE.
A posted total is NOT the market's expectation -- the price tells you which
side of the line the expectation sits on. '88.5, over -130 / under +105'
means the market thinks 88.5 is low. Taking the line at face value throws
that away, and the discarded information is worth up to about a win and a
half. Wins are Binomial(162, p), so with an outcome SD of ~6.35:
true_mean = line + 6.35 * Phi^-1( P(over), de-vigged )
Both sides are needed to de-vig properly. A bare line still works and is
read as-is, which is the honest fallback when the juice is unknown.
WHAT IT FEEDS:
wins -> save and hold opportunity pools (team_wins.py)
wins -> run differential -> the RS/RA magnitude
It does NOT set the RS/RA split. A 95-win club could be 5.2 RS / 4.2 RA or
4.3 / 3.3 and the market price is identical either way. The market supplies
the magnitude of the run differential; the bottom-up roster factors supply
how it divides between offense and defense.
FIELDS:
market        'win_total' (default), 'division', 'pennant', or
'world_series'.
odds_format   'american' (-130 / +105), 'decimal', or 'probability'.
Applies to the over/under prices, and to futures prices.
teams         team code -> either a bare line (96.5) or an object
{line, over, under}. Any code canonical_team() understands
works. Give ALL 30 clubs: a partial board warns, because
the teams left out fall back to the bottom-up projection
and the two scales then mix.
as_of / book  free text, for provenance. Record when you pulled the board
and from where -- totals move across an offseason and a
stale board is worse than none.
ONE BIAS THIS DOES NOT CORRECT: large-market clubs carry lines a touch
higher than talent alone justifies. Read a big-market club's
market-implied wins as a mild over-estimate.
The numbers below are ILLUSTRATIVE PLACEHOLDERS showing the shape and
rough spread of a real board. They are not a forecast and are not pulled
from any book. Replace all 30 before using this.
